hook: Lightning hit their Moon rocket 36 seconds after liftoff.
narration: Thirty six seconds after liftoff, lightning struck this Moon rocket.
It was Apollo 12, November 1969, with Pete Conrad, Richard Gordon and Alan Bean aboard.
The Saturn Five had lifted off in the driving rain.
Inside the capsule, the crew asked what had happened as systems dropped out.
In space and on the ground, they checked everything to be sure the lightning had not damaged anything that would endanger the mission.
A rocket and its long exhaust plume can trigger lightning when it climbs through a charged cloud.
Five days after launch, Conrad steered the lunar module down to the surface with ten percent fuel showing.
outcome: Apollo 12 landed as close as possible to its target, the old Surveyor probe, and the crew splashed down safely back on Earth.
title: Lightning hit Apollo 12 at liftoff
question_comment: Would you have kept flying to the Moon after a lightning strike?

description:
Apollo 12 is struck by lightning 36 seconds after lifting off in the rain at Kennedy Space Center on Nov. 14, 1969, and goes on to a pinpoint landing beside the Surveyor probe on the Moon.
